description: The Orbital Debris Quarterly News is the newsletter of NASA's Orbital Debris Program Office at Johnson Space Center, published since 1996 with each issue as a downloadable PDF. The archive page read on 2026-09-28 describes it as covering the latest events in orbital debris research, news and statistics, project reviews and meeting reports, and lists issues up to July 2026, which reports radar measurements of the debris environment in 2024 and 2025 from the HUSIR and Goldstone radars together with the regular charts of the monthly number of objects in Earth orbit by object type and the satellite box score by country; the September 2025 issue covers an updated explosion rate method for long-term debris modelling and an overview of the catalogued population. Coverage is global, from 1996 to 2026. Access is free; no licence is stated on the page. Caveats: statistics come as charts and tables inside PDF issues, so series have to be extracted, and counts are revised as cataloguing continues. It supports space infrastructure risk studies, such as tracking the growth of the orbital population that threatens navigation and communication satellites. Related records: NASA's fragmentation history, the ORDEM debris engineering model and the CelesTrak satellite catalogue.
